title: Clock faces & Llama-3.2-1B
blurb: Every five minutes round the clock, 144 times. One view is a drawn clock face (48×48 pixels, softly blurred): the hands go round, so 11:55 sits right next to 12:00. The other is Llama-3.2-1B reading the time as text, “The meeting starts at 3:15.” (layer 8, averaged over 6 sentences). Does the model know the clock goes round?

notes.neighbors: To the pixels, 11:55’s nearest neighbour is 11:00: the same two hands, swapped. Llama-3.2-1B instead files every time under its hour; the minutes barely move it.
notes.cloud: Llama-3.2-1B lays the hours out like a number line, 1, 2, 3 … 11, 12, with 12 at the far end beside 11 rather than just before 1. It reads “12:00” as a number, not as the top of a dial.

about.name: Llama-3.2-1B
about.quote: The Llama 3.2 collection of multilingual large language models (LLMs) is a collection of pretrained and instruction-tuned generative models in 1B and 3B sizes (text in/text out).
about.label: Meta model card

here: Here: the 144 times from 12:00 to 11:55 in five-minute steps, as a drawn 48×48 analog clock face, softly blurred (A), and as Llama-3.2-1B layer-8 states for the time written as text, averaged over six sentences like “The meeting starts at 3:15.” (B).

llama3.text: Grattafiori, Dubey, et al. (2024). The Llama 3 Herd of Models. arXiv:2407.21783.
